title: The development of understanding of genetics and evolution

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Extinction
items.clue: No individuals of a species remain alive.

items.label: Evolutionary tree
items.clue: A branching diagram showing common ancestors.

items.label: MRSA
items.clue: A strain of bacteria which is resistant to antibiotics.

items.label: Variation
items.clue: The differences between individuals of the same species.

questions.stem: In a beetle population, shell thickness varies. Predators cannot eat the thickest-shelled beetles. After many generations most beetles have thick shells. Why?

options.text: Beetles grew thicker shells in life and passed them on.
Thick-shelled beetles survived to breed and passed this on.
Beetles needed thicker shells, so they grew them to survive.
Predators made thick shells appear in the beetle population.

questions.explanation: Individuals with characteristics most suited to the environment are more likely to survive to breed successfully, and the characteristics that have enabled these individuals to survive are then passed on to the next generation.

questions.stem: What was Alfred Russel Wallace's contribution to the theory of evolution by natural selection?

options.text: He collected specimens overseas for Darwin's new book.
He explained natural selection using genes and DNA.
He proposed the same theory independently of Darwin.
He convinced other scientists to accept the theory.

questions.explanation: Alfred Russel Wallace independently proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection and published joint writings with Darwin in 1858, which prompted Darwin to publish On the Origin of Species the following year.

questions.stem: Which of these is a reason why the theory of evolution by natural selection was only gradually accepted?

options.text: Scientists in 1859 were at once convinced by the evidence.
The mechanism of inheritance was not known for 50 more years.
Lamarck had shown that changes made in life are inherited.
Darwin had already explained inheritance in terms of genes.

questions.explanation: The mechanism of inheritance and variation was not known until 50 years after the theory was published, which is one of the reasons given for the theory being only gradually accepted.

questions.stem: Which statement about the theory of speciation is correct?

options.text: More evidence has changed our understanding over time.
Wallace gathered the evidence for Darwin's own ideas.
Two groups are new species once they look different.
Wallace's ideas on speciation were accepted at once.

questions.explanation: Alfred Wallace did much pioneering work on speciation but more evidence over time has led to our current understanding of the theory of speciation.

questions.stem: Giraffes with longer necks can reach more leaves. How would a biologist today explain why giraffes now have long necks?

options.text: Reaching high leaves created the long neck characteristic.
Necks stretched during life were passed to the offspring.
Giraffes needed longer necks, so their necks became longer.
Giraffes with longer necks survived and bred more often.

questions.explanation: Individuals with characteristics most suited to the environment are more likely to survive to breed successfully, and those characteristics are then passed on to the next generation.

questions.stem: Two populations of one snail species are separated by a new river. What must finally happen for them to become two different species?

options.text: They must look different enough to be told apart by eye.
They must change during life and pass these changes on.
They must not be able to breed to give fertile young.
The river must create new characteristics in each group.

questions.explanation: The isolated populations experience different conditions, so natural selection selects different characteristics in each. Over many generations they become so different that they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring, and they are then two species.
